newsitem.title: USA: Japan promoting ties with Asia on forex -Kubo.
newsitem.headline: Japan promoting ties with Asia on forex -Kubo.

text.p: Japan's monetary authorities are moving towards promoting cooperative ties with its Asian counterparts for the stability of global foreign exchange markets, Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Tuesday.
Kubo, speaking at the annual meeting of International Monetary Fund and World Bank, said in a speech that currency stability was a common goal of world economies.
Cooperation in currency markets among industrialised nations since the Plaza Accord should also be expanded to include new and emerging markets of Asia, he added.
"From this standpoint, our monetary authorities are moving towards tie-ups with the monetary authorities of Asian Pacific nations," he said.

Foreign reserves among Asian nations make up for about 40 percent of the world's total. He said it was necessary to join hands with emerging nations to strengthen ability to deal with various risks in the international monetary markets.

As one step towards this aim, Kubo said he welcomed the creation of the expanded General Arrangement to Borrow (GAB) facility, known as the New Arrangement to Borrow (NAB) which includes other nations beside Group of 10 countries.

Allocation of artificial currency, Special Drawing Rights (SDR), to the IMF's newest members and contributions to boost the fund's resources is another way to establish rights and responsibilities of emerging and so-called "transition" countries like Russia, he said.

Emerging nations in Asia and Latin America need to make improvements on their capital markets and to fine-tune their accounting and legal rules to encourage the influx of private funds into their infrastructure projets, Kubo said.

As for debt-ridden poor nations, Japan stands ready to help them on a bilateral basis. Japan will comply with conditions set by the Paris Club creditors to relieve debt as much as 80 percent from the 67 percent ceiling now, after "substantial progress" is made by the international organisations to come up with an overall debt-relief scheme, Kubo said.

Japan's economy is continuing to recover with brightness emerging in private sector demand such as private consumption, capital spendings and housing construction. The government will steadily implement this fiscal year's budget and cope with problem loans to strengthen its economic recovery, he said.
Tokyo is also continuing its easy monetary policy by maintaining the official discount rate at five percent.
"We will act appropriately with flexibility while watching economies and financal markets both at home and abroad in forming our monetary policy," Kubo said.
He stressed the importance for industrialised nations to reduce deficit for continual growth without inflation and expressed hopes that emerging nations would contribute to global growth.
